Synopsis:
Bank of Israel Deputy Governor Andrew Abir signaled further rate cuts are possible after a third consecutive cut brought the benchmark rate to 3.25%, a near four-year low. The driver is below-midpoint inflation (1.5% in July vs. 1%-3% target), aided by shekel strength. Future cuts remain data-dependent; the central bank's own forecast has a floor of 3% by mid-2027. Geopolitical risk remains a wildcard, though Israel's risk premium and CDS spreads have normalized to pre-Gaza war levels.
